questions.question: What is used to classify a real symmetric matrix as definite, semidefinite, or indefinite?
options: The order of elementary row operations

questions.question: What does it mean for a quadratic form to be indefinite?
options: It is positive for every nonzero vector
It is undefined for some coordinates
It takes both positive and negative values
It is zero for every vector

questions.question: Which condition is part of the positive definite case?
options: $x^TAx \lt 0$ for at least one vector only

questions.question: Why is symmetry mentioned for definiteness here?
options: The classification is stated for real symmetric matrices
Nonsymmetric matrices cannot be multiplied by vectors

questions.question: How can eigenvalues help with definiteness for symmetric matrices?
options: Only their order in a list matters
Their signs determine the definiteness class
Their eigenvectors are ignored because signs cannot be used
They replace the need for the matrix to be square

questions.question: Classify $I_n$ using definiteness.
Classify $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$.
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$, what is the definiteness class?
options: Positive semidefinite but not positive definite

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, which classification fits best?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}-2&0\\0&-5\end{pmatrix}$, what is the definiteness class?
What is the difference between positive definite and positive semidefinite?
options: Positive definite is strictly positive; semidefinite allows zero
Positive definite allows negative values only once.
There is no difference for symmetric matrices

questions.question: Why does one negative value of $x^TAx$ rule out positive semidefiniteness?
options: Positive semidefinite only checks one vector
The zero vector must give a negative value
Negative values are allowed if the determinant is positive
Positive semidefinite requires $x^TAx\ge0$ for every vector

questions.question: For a symmetric matrix with eigenvalues $2$, $0$, and $5$, what does the zero eigenvalue prevent?
Classify $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ by the signs of $x^TAx$.
A symmetric matrix has eigenvalues $-1$ and $4$. What is its definiteness class?
A symmetric matrix has eigenvalues $-2$ and $-3$. What is its definiteness class?
Why is checking only $x=e_1$ and $x=e_2$ not enough to prove definiteness in general?
options: Standard basis vectors are not allowed in quadratic forms
Mixed directions can reveal different signs through cross terms
Definiteness ignores all vectors except basis vectors
The zero vector is the only vector that matters

questions.question: What does a single zero value at a nonzero vector rule out?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, which two vectors show that $A$ is indefinite?
A symmetric matrix has eigenvalues $0$, $0$, and $7$. Which classification is correct?
options: Positive semidefinite but not positive definite
